REFUTED: Today on this worktree, 5 of 88 live-vs-repo rule files are byte-identical, 25 repo-larger, 3 live-larger.

A second live tree is how operators hot-patch a rule without waiting for a repo commit. Collapsing to one tree removes that operational valve. Detection-after-the-fact (Stop-hook warning) keeps the valve and still surfaces drift, which can be enough on a single-owner estate. That counterargument survives as an operational preference; it does not make two trees structurally consistent, and it does not restore the 2026-08-09 5/88 numbers on this Linux worktree where both host trees are absent.
Config-first minimises surprise execution of unreviewed files; it does not minimise surprise absence of on-disk capabilities.
A file is loaded by A1 only if it is listed in MANIFEST.json.
Absence of a generator removes a class of detectors; it does not remove the orphan-on-disk failure class.
A1 is a minimal (fewest-moving-parts) config-first control plane, not a proof that it is the lowest-risk of the nine classes.
